subject: Invoice ingestion: handling non-UTF8 characters & PO reference mapping
messages:
From: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@lumensupply.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@lumensupply.com
Date: 2028-06-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Vendor onboarding: invoice template + character issues

Hi Logan,

Thanks for sending over the onboarding packet earlier. We're getting our finance team to convert historic invoices to the new format but we've hit two issues we wanted to flag before go-live:

1) Encoding: some legacy invoices contain ISO-8859-1 characters (curly quotes, em‑dashes) and a few line items include emoji-like characters from legacy ERPs. Our CSV exporter currently emits those as windows-1252. Can Redwood's portal ingest non-UTF8 or do we need to normalize to UTF-8?

2) PO mapping: our PO references sometimes appear in the invoice filename and sometimes in a free-text "Notes" column. We want to avoid duplicated/missed matching. Is there a preferred canonical field Redwood will use to match POs (PO_Number, PO_Ref, or filename token)?

Attached is a small sample CSV (sample_invoice_utf8.csv) and the vendor onboarding form (vendor_onboarding_form.pdf).

Short ask: what should we normalize on our side to minimize errors? Are you comfortable accepting email ingestion for a small pilot while we finish portal provisioning?

Best,
Elena
Finance Ops | Lumensupply

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@lumensupply.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-03T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: invoice template + character issues

Hi Elena — thanks for the samples and the clear note. A few quick points and a proposed pilot approach: 

- Encoding: our portal and ingestion pipeline expect UTF-8. We can accept windows-1252 / ISO-8859-1 as an email fallback, but we will convert to UTF-8 on ingest. If there are bytes that don't map cleanly we currently flag them as "encoding error" and surface the file to AP for manual review. For a clean pilot, if you can provide a UTF-8 export that avoids control characters we'll see far fewer manual exceptions.

- PO mapping: canonical field we use is PO_Number (single column). If PO appears only in filename we will attempt an automatic extraction, but filename parsing is brittle. If you have a reliable Notes->PO pattern we can add a preprocessing rule, but default priority is PO_Number column -> PO_Ref -> filename.

Pilot proposal:
1) Portal provisioning takes ~3 business days.
2) While portal is being set up, we'll accept email-submitted CSVs to accounts-payable@redwood.com with the subject token: "PO-TOKEN:<PO_NUMBER>" (this lets us route and idempotently match).
3) You should normalize to UTF-8 if possible; otherwise include a header column "Encoding" and set it to "windows-1252" so our parser knows to run the conversion heuristics.

I've attached a small mapping workbook (po-field-mapping.xlsx) template and will loop in Kimberly to confirm the column-to-ledger mapping.

If that works, can you confirm a pilot batch (10 invoices) sent tomorrow?

Thanks,
Logan
Senior Ops Program Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@lumensupply.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: accounts-payable@lumensupply.com
Date: 2028-06-04T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: invoice template + character issues

Thanks Logan — that flow is helpful. A couple clarifications from AP:

- We can emit UTF-8 CSVs but our legacy export uses windows-1252 by default. Adding an "Encoding" header is straightforward so we'll do that for the pilot.
- The team prefers the subject token approach for email fallback. We'll send the pilot 10 invoices to accounts-payable@redwood.com with subjects like: 
  "PO-TOKEN: 38752"

Attached sample shows two tricky cases: invoice line with “smart quotes” and a description field with an ampersand and a non-breaking space. Please confirm those will round-trip.

—Elena

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@lumensupply.com>
Date: 2028-06-05T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: invoice template + character issues

Elena — quick mapping confirmation from our side:

- We'll map PO_Number -> Redwood_PO (string).
- If PO_Number is empty, we'll attempt PO_Ref, and then filename extraction as a last resort.
- For the pilot I set a tolerance rule: if encoding conversion yields replacement characters (�) the invoice will be routed to "AP Exceptions" and flagged for manual correction instead of auto-posting.

Operational asks:
- Please include the vendor_tax_id column on the CSV to disambiguate multi-entity cases.
- For email pilot, include only one invoice per email to ensure idempotency when retries happen.

We'll monitor the first 10 and provide a report by end of day Monday. If all good, we'll flip portal provisioning live and retire the email fallback.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
AP Integrations Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Elena Suarez <elena.suarez@lumensupply.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-06T14:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor onboarding: invoice template + character issues

Hi Elena — quick operational notes before pilot:

- Please use the subject token exactly as: PO-TOKEN:<PO_NUMBER> (no spaces around colon). Examples that will route correctly: "PO-TOKEN:38752" or "PO-TOKEN:AB-1234".
- File attachments should be CSV (not XLSX) for email fallback. If you must send PDF invoices, attach the PDF and include a single CSV with the fields we outlined (PO_Number, vendor_tax_id, invoice_date, amount, line_items).
- Do not put multiple invoices in a single CSV for the pilot; split them into one-row files to reduce parsing ambiguity.

I'll watch the queue and ping once the first batch arrives. Thanks for moving quickly on the Encoding header.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Revenue Ops | Redwood Inference
